chunks: By this chain of transmission, from Bakr ibn Abdullah, who said: Muhammad ibn Ubaydullah and Abdullah ibn al-Salt al-Juhdari narrated to us. They both said: Ibn A'isha narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Hamadani, from his father, who said:
When Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them both) buried Fatima, he stood at the edge of the grave — this was in the middle of the night, for he had buried her at night — then he began to recite:

For every gathering of two intimate friends there is a parting, / And all that is done before death is brief. / Indeed my loss of one person after another / Is an indication that no intimate friend endures. / My memory will be turned away from, and my love forgotten, / And after me, the intimate friend will find another intimate friend.

key_terms.افْتِقَاد: Iftiqad — bereavement, the loss of a beloved person
key_terms.جَوْفُ اللَّيْلِ: The depth/middle of the night — emphasizing the secrecy and solemnity of the burial
key_terms.خَلِيل: Khalil — intimate friend or beloved, a term denoting the deepest form of human love and friendship
key_terms.شَفِيرُ الْقَبْرِ: The edge/rim of the grave — a poignant image of the bereaved standing at the precipice of separation
key_terms.فُرْقَة: Furqa — separation, the inevitable parting that follows every meeting

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali recite at the grave of Fatima al-Zahra?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Amali of Sheikh al-Saduq records the moment Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS) buried his wife Sayyida Fatima al-Zahra (AS) secretly at night, following her wish. Standing at her graveside alone in the darkness, he expressed his profound grief through three couplets of classical Arabic poetry — a genre known as ritha' (elegy). The poem meditates on the transient nature of human companionship and the inevitability of separation, reflecting the depth of his love and his Stoic acceptance of mortality. The secret night burial of Fatima (AS) is a historically significant event in early Islamic history, reflecting the political tensions of the early caliphate period.

en.bilal-muhammad: By this isnad from Bakr b. `Abdullah. He said: Muhammad b. `Ubaydullah and `Abdullah b. al-Salt al-Juhdari narrated to us. They said: Ibn `A’isha narrated to us from `Abdullah b. `Abd al-Rahman al-Hamadani from his father. He said:
When `Ali b. Abi Talib buried Fatima (sa), he stood at the edge of the grave. This was in the middle of the night because he had buried her at night. Then, he recited:

For every meeting between two lovers there is a departure, And all that is done [together] before death is brief, My loss of one person after the other Is an indication that the lover is not everlasting, My remembrance will cease, and my love will be forgotten, And my lover will have a lover after me.
